children: WALL STREET SWINGS FOR GAINS AND MISSES AS OIL, TREASURY YIELDS CLIMB

US stocks moved lower straight out of the gate on Thursday and spent the entire session trying to claw their way back to green, paring losses throughout the session amid signs of progress in peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
That was easier said than done, with rising fuel prices keeping inflation worries front and center, and US Treasury yields touching multi-year highs.
The Nasdaq eked out a nominal gain, while the S&P 500 logged a slight decline. The Dow was the laggard, closing down 0.3%.
US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the economic blockade, according to sources close to the talks.
Even so, the Iran-backed Houthi's missle attach on Saudi Arabia sent oil prices higher and exacerbated the global bond selloff, sending the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield
as high as 5.223% and pushing 30-year T-bond yields to their highest level since the last episode of "Friends" aired (2004).
Front month WTI
and Brent (LOCc1) crude prices settled up 2.7% and 2.4% on the day.

In Fed news, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammock and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson both indicated that the inflation fight is far from over and additional rate hikes are probably waiting in the wings.

In Washington, the Trump-Xi summit got underway with a mix of high pomp and low expectations, other than stabilizing an often rocky relationship between the world's two largest economies. Tariffs, technology, rare earth minerals and the flow of oil from the Middle East are among topics likely to be swatted around the room.
On the sector level, communication services
and travel/leisure (.SPCOMHOTL) were among the outperformers, while gold & silver miners (.XAU), Dow Transports
, utilities
and materials
ended the session with the steepest percentage losses.
Chips
declined but FANGS
advanced, and growth (.IGX) topped value

On Friday, the Trump-Xi show continues, the Commerce Department is due to release its August report on new orders for US-made durable goods, and the University of Michigan will take its second and final stab at September consumer sentiment.
Here's your closing snapshot:
Nasdaq ekes out nominal gain, S&P 500 ends slightly lower, Dow ends off 0.3%
Utilities down most among S&P 500 sectors; communications services lead gainers
Dollar rises, bitcoin flat; US crude rallies >3%; gold dips
US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~5.22%
